units: <cite ref="Mishnah Nedarim 10:2">Ned. X, 2</cite>, v. <cite ref="T00441"><he>רוֹקֵן</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 67">Gen. R. s. 67</cite> <he>ששה … ברְשׁוּתוֹ שלשה אינן ברשותו</he> six things (organs) serve man, three of which are under his control, and three are not; <he>העין … ורשותו וכ׳</he> the eye, the ear, and the nose are not under his control &c.

Bets. V, 2 משום ר׳ as an exercise of authority (judging, betrothal &c.; differ. interpret. in comment.); a. fr.—Esp. secular government, (mostly) the Roman government in Palestine, Roman officials, Roman party.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 1:10">Ab. I, 10</cite>, v. <cite ref="J00106"><he>יָדַע</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 2:3">Ib. II, 3</cite>, v. <cite ref="G00097"><he>זָהִיר</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Shabbat 11a:5">Sabb. 11ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="H01078"><he>חָלָל</he> III</cite>.

<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 17a:7">Ab. Zar. 17ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Proverbs 30:15">Prov. XXX, 15</cite>) <he>קול שתי בנות … ומאי נינהי מינות והר׳</he> Ms. M. the voice of two daughters that cry from Gehenna, and say in this world, ‘bring, bring’; and who are they? Heresy and Government.
<cite ref="Mishnah Makhshirin 2:5">Makhsh. II, 5</cite> <he>אם יש בה ר׳</he> if it is the residence of Roman officials (for whom the baths are always kept in readiness).
<cite ref="Yoma 86b:18">Yoma 86ᵇ</cite> <he>והר׳ מקברת וכ׳</he> and high office buries its occupant (causes premature death).

Erub. 41ᵇ שלשה אין רואין … חולי מעיין והר׳ three persons shall not see Gehenna (expiate their sins in this world): those who suffer from extreme poverty, from bowel diseases, and from governmental exactions (Rashi: from creditors).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 6:10:4">Y. Snh. VI, 23ᵈ</cite> sq. <he>ר׳ של מטן</he> the earthly government; <he>ר׳ של מעלן</he> the divine government; a. fr.—Pl. <he>רְשׁוּיוֹת</he>.

<cite ref="Chagigah 15a:5">Ḥag. 15ᵃ</cite> <he>שמא … שתי ר׳ הן</he> are there, God forbid! two powers (governing the universe)? <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 1:10">Gen. R. s. 1</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="B01157"><he>ברא</he></cite>, <cite ref="Genesis 1:1">Gen. I, 1</cite>) <he>אין כל … שתי ר׳ וכ׳</he> none can say, two powers created the world (the verb <cite ref="B01157"><he>ברא</he></cite> being in the singular) &c.
<cite ref="Berakhot 33b:17">Ber. 33ᵇ</cite> <he>דמיחזי כשתי ר׳</he> (saying <cite ref="M00410"><he>מודים</he></cite> twice) has the appearance of a belief in a duality; a. e.

<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 1:2">B. Kam. I, 2</cite> <he>ר׳ המיוחדת למזיק</he> a territory exclusively belonging to the owner of the animal that did the damage; <he>ר׳ הניזק והמזיק</he> a space belonging to both owners. Ib. 13ᵇ (in Chald. dict.) <he>תורך ברְשׁוּתִי מאי בעי</he> what had thy ox to do in my ground. Ib. 81ᵃ; <cite ref="Taanit 6b">Taan. 6ᵇ</cite> <he>שבילי הר׳</he> the paths (short cuts) through private property.
B. Mets. 5ᵇ משביעין אותו שבועה שאינו ברשותו we make him swear that it is not in his possession; a. v. fr.—ר׳ היחיד (abbrev. רהי֞) private ground; ר׳ הרבים (abbrev. רהר֞, רה֞) public road.
<cite ref="Shabbat 6a:16">Sabb. 6ᵃ</cite>; a. v. fr.—

Ib. 9ᵃ הרי זו ר׳ לעצמה this forms a territory for itself (with regard to Sabbath movements). Ib. VII, 2 המוציא מר׳ לר׳ he who carries things (on the Sabbath) from one territory to another; a. fr.—Pl. as ab. Ib. 6ᵃ ארבע ר׳ לשבת וכ׳ there are four classes of territories with regard to Sabbath laws &c.; Tosef. ib. I, 1. Ib. 6; Sabb. l. c. אסקופה … שתי ר׳ the threshold stands for two territories; when the door is open, it is classified with the interior &c. Ib. 9ᵃ כל … מוצא שתי ר׳ וכ׳ wherever you find two territories belonging to the same class; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 3:9:3">Y. Kidd. III, 64ᶜ</cite> top; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim 8:1:2">Y. Ned. VIII, 40ᵈ</cite> bot. (ref. to R. Jose’s opinions <cite ref="Mishnah Kiddushin 3:9">Kidd. III, 9</cite>, a.

<cite ref="Mishnah Nedarim 8:2">Ned. VIII, 2</cite>) <he>תמן הוא אמר עד שיצאו כל הרשויות הגדולות עד שיצאו כל הר׳ הקטנות וכ׳</he> there, he says, the terms, ‘the oldest’, ‘the youngest’, tend to exclude all the older daughters, and all the younger daughters respectively (so that only the oldest of the daughters of his first wife, and respectively the youngest of the daughters of his second wife are meant), and here he says so (that the widest scope is adopted)?
<cite ref="Berakhot 28a:2">Ber. 28ᵃ</cite> <he>וניתנה להם ר׳ וכ׳</he> and permission to enter was given to the students.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 3:15">Ab. III, 15</cite>, v. <cite ref="R00672"><he>צָפָה</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Chullin 141a:7">Ḥull. 141ᵃ</cite> <he>לדבר הר׳</he>, v. <cite ref="M02284"><he>מִצְוָה</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Chullin 106a:14">Ib. 106ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="M02284"><he>מִצְוָה</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Berakhot 27b:17">Ber. 27ᵇ</cite>, v. <cite ref="H00242"><he>חוֹבָה</he></cite>.
M. Kat. III, 3 אגרות של ר׳, v. שְׁאִילָה; a. fr.—נטילת ר׳ taking leave of absence, parting, at which a religious remark was customary.

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 17:5">Lev. R. s. 17</cite> <he>עביד להו נ׳ ר</he> made these verses the text for leave-taking (cmp. <cite ref="A02665"><he>אַפְטַרְתָּא</he></cite>). Y. Ber. II, 5ᶜ bot. <he>ההיא מילתא … הוה נ׳ ר׳ דידיה</he> that remark … was his leave-taking.—[
<cite ref="Eruvin 41b">Erub. 41ᵇ</cite>, v. supra.]
